response: {"scenarios":[{"id":1,"title":"The Overbooked Day","difficulty":2,"narrative":"You wake up to a day that was supposed to be manageable, but your phone immediately starts buzzing. Your boss emails you about a 'quick' project due by noon, your partner asks if you can pick up groceries for a dinner party tonight, and your support group chat is blowing up with someone in crisis. You feel the familiar tightness in your chest as the to-do list triples in seconds. The morning sun is shining, but your mind is already racing to catch up.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Reply to your boss that you'll get to the project after you've made a prioritized list, text your partner that you can help but need them to handle one other errand, and mute the group chat for one hour to focus.","strategy":"Analytical"},{"id":"B","text":"Take three deep breaths, acknowledge that you're feeling overwhelmed, and remind yourself that you don't have to solve everything at once. Then, tackle the most urgent task first.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"},{"id":"C","text":"Immediately say yes to everything to avoid disappointing anyone, and try to multitask by working on the project while shopping and texting support simultaneously.","strategy":"People-Pleasing"},{"id":"D","text":"Put your phone on Do Not Disturb, pull the covers back over your head, and tell yourself you'll deal with it all later.","strategy":"Avoidant"}]},{"id":2,"title":"The Misunderstood Message","difficulty":2,"narrative":"You send a carefully written message to a close friend, sharing something personal about your week. They reply with a short 'K.' You stare at the screen, your mind instantly spinning stories: Are they mad? Did you say something wrong? The silence feels loud, and you feel a knot forming in your stomach as you reread your original message over and over.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Send a follow-up message asking if they're upset, explaining that their short reply made you anxious, and clarifying what you meant.","strategy":"Assertive Communication"},{"id":"B","text":"Remind yourself that a short reply doesn't necessarily mean anger—they might just be busy. Put your phone away and do something grounding.","strategy":"Cognitive Reframing"},{"id":"C","text":"Decide they're clearly mad and start drafting an apology message for something you're not even sure you did wrong.","strategy":"Self-Blame"},{"id":"D","text":"Assume the friendship is falling apart and start distancing yourself from them before they can reject you further.","strategy":"Avoidant"}]},{"id":3,"title":"The Unexpected Bill","difficulty":2,"narrative":"You open your mailbox and find an unexpected bill that's larger than you anticipated. It's not catastrophic, but it throws off your carefully planned monthly budget. Your heart rate picks up as you mentally recalculate your finances. The rational part of your brain knows it's manageable, but the anxious part is already catastrophizing about what else could go wrong.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Sit down, review your full budget, and create a realistic plan to cover the bill without panicking. You've handled surprises before.","strategy":"Analytical"},{"id":"B","text":"Notice the anxiety rising, take a few grounding breaths, and remind yourself that this is a solvable problem—not an emergency.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"},{"id":"C","text":"Immediately put the bill on a credit card and worry about it next month, hoping it all works out.","strategy":"Avoidant"},{"id":"D","text":"Call a friend to vent about how unfair the bill is, seeking validation for your frustration before taking any action.","strategy":"Social Support"}]},{"id":4,"title":"The Group Plan Pressure","difficulty":2,"narrative":"Your friends are planning a weekend trip and everyone is excited. They're looking at you for confirmation that you're in. You've been looking forward to a quiet weekend to recharge, but you also don't want to be the one who ruins the group's fun. The group chat is full of enthusiasm, and you feel the weight of their expectations pressing down on you.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Honestly tell your friends that you need a recharge weekend this time, but suggest a specific date when you'd love to join them.","strategy":"Assertive"},{"id":"B","text":"Acknowledge your need for rest, but agree to go anyway because saying no feels too uncomfortable.","strategy":"People-Pleasing"},{"id":"C","text":"Ignore the group chat entirely and hope the plans finalize without you needing to respond.","strategy":"Avoidant"},{"id":"D","text":"Take a moment to check in with yourself about what you truly need, then make a decision based on your energy levels rather than guilt.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"}]},{"id":5,"title":"The Work Email Spiral","difficulty":2,"narrative":"You receive an email from a colleague that feels slightly passive-aggressive. It's not overtly rude, but the tone makes you uneasy. You read it three times, analyzing every word. Your stress is already high, and this email feels like it could be the start of a conflict you don't have the energy for.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Reply calmly and professionally, asking for clarification on the points you're unsure about, without assuming negative intent.","strategy":"Assertive"},{"id":"B","text":"Step away from the email for 30 minutes, do a grounding exercise, and return to it with fresh eyes before responding.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"},{"id":"C","text":"Assume the worst, start drafting a defensive reply, and consider forwarding it to your manager preemptively.","strategy":"Catastrophizing"},{"id":"D","text":"Delete the email and pretend you never saw it, hoping the issue resolves itself.","strategy":"Avoidant"}]},{"id":6,"title":"The Social Media Comparison","difficulty":2,"narrative":"You're scrolling through social media and see a post from someone you know announcing a major life achievement—a promotion, a new relationship, a dream vacation. A familiar wave of comparison washes over you. Your own progress feels small and insignificant in comparison. The glow of the screen reflects your slightly deflated expression.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Remind yourself that social media is a highlight reel, reflect on your own recent wins (even small ones), and consider taking a break from the app.","strategy":"Cognitive Reframing"},{"id":"B","text":"Close the app immediately, put your phone in another room, and go for a short walk to reset your mood.","strategy":"Behavioral Disengagement"},{"id":"C","text":"Double down on scrolling, comparing yourself to more people, and letting the envy build until you feel motivated by it.","strategy":"Negative Comparison"},{"id":"D","text":"Post something yourself to try to get validation and likes to feel better about your own situation.","strategy":"External Validation"}]},{"id":7,"title":"The Family Gathering","difficulty":2,"narrative":"You're heading to a family dinner where a relative tends to ask intrusive questions about your life—your job, your relationships, your plans. You've been doing well managing your anxiety, but the thought of being put on the spot in front of everyone makes your palms sweat. You park outside the house and take a moment before walking in.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Prepare a few polite but firm boundary phrases in advance, like 'I'd rather not get into that tonight, but thanks for asking!'","strategy":"Assertive"},{"id":"B","text":"Take a moment to ground yourself, remind yourself that their questions reflect their curiosity—not your worth—and set an intention to stay calm.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"},{"id":"C","text":"Answer every question in detail to avoid any awkward silence or judgment, even if it makes you uncomfortable.","strategy":"People-Pleasing"},{"id":"D","text":"Cancel last minute with an excuse and stay home, relieved to avoid the situation entirely.","strategy":"Avoidant"}]},{"id":8,"title":"The Sleep Disruption","difficulty":2,"narrative":"It's 2:00 AM and you're wide awake. Tomorrow is an important day—a presentation, a meeting, or an event you've been preparing for. Your mind is running through everything that could go wrong. You check the clock every few minutes, each time feeling more anxious about losing sleep. The darkness of your room feels heavy.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Get out of bed, go to another room, do something calming like reading or light stretching until you feel sleepy, then return to bed.","strategy":"Analytical"},{"id":"B","text":"Stay in bed but practice a body scan meditation or 4-7-8 breathing technique to calm your nervous system.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"},{"id":"C","text":"Grab your phone and start scrolling to pass the time, telling yourself you'll fall asleep eventually.","strategy":"Avoidant"},{"id":"D","text":"Start mentally rehearsing tomorrow's event in detail, convinced that extra preparation will make up for lost sleep.","strategy":"Overthinking"}]},{"id":9,"title":"The Support Group Trigger","difficulty":2,"narrative":"During your support group session, someone shares a story that closely mirrors a painful experience you've had. You weren't expecting it, and suddenly you feel your throat tighten and your eyes sting. Everyone is listening intently, and you're trying to hold it together. The facilitator hasn't noticed your reaction yet.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Allow yourself to feel the emotion without judgment, use a grounding technique like pressing your feet into the floor, and share only if you feel ready.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"},{"id":"B","text":"Raise your hand and let the facilitator know you need a moment, then step outside briefly to collect yourself before returning.","strategy":"Assertive"},{"id":"C","text":"Suppress the emotion completely, keep a neutral face, and never mention it—not even after the session.","strategy":"Avoidant"},{"id":"D","text":"Immediately start sharing your own story in detail to connect with the person, even if you're not emotionally ready to process it publicly.","strategy":"Emotional Flooding"}]},{"id":10,"title":"The Decision Crossroads","difficulty":2,"narrative":"You're faced with two choices: one is safe and familiar but doesn't excite you; the other is uncertain but aligns with something you've been wanting to try—a new hobby class, a social event outside your comfort zone, or a small personal challenge. Your anxiety is whispering all the reasons to stay safe, but a small part of you is curious about the unknown path. The clock is ticking on your decision.","options":[{"id":"A","text":"Make a pros-and-cons list, weigh the realistic risks, and give yourself a deadline to decide without overthinking.","strategy":"Analytical"},{"id":"B","text":"Acknowledge the anxiety without letting it decide for you. Choose the uncertain path, knowing that growth lives outside your comfort zone.","strategy":"Emotionally Regulated"},{"id":"C","text":"Choose the safe option immediately because the anxiety of uncertainty is too uncomfortable to sit with.","strategy":"Avoidant"},{"id":"D","text":"Ask three different friends what they would do and go with the majority opinion to avoid responsibility for the choice.","strategy":"External Validation"}]}]}
